Settings.Game.Intro: Where the game, its settings and the other tools are. Each is found by itself when it can be; set one when it isn't, or to use another.
Settings.Game.GameFolderAbout: Where The Witcher 3 is installed: its bundles, scripts, mods and DLC. It's found in your Steam and GOG libraries when this is empty.
Settings.Game.GameFolderFindTip: Look for The Witcher 3 in your Steam and GOG libraries
Settings.Game.GameNotFound: Not set, and the game wasn't found in your Steam or GOG libraries. Set it to read the game's files and scripts.
Settings.Game.GameFoundUsed: Not set, so the one found is used: {folder}
Settings.Game.GameFound: Found the game's files and scripts.
Settings.Game.GameWrongFolder: This isn't The Witcher 3 folder. Choose the one that has the bin and content folders.
Settings.Game.GameMissing: It isn't in your Steam or GOG libraries. Use the folder button to pick it yourself.
Settings.Game.DocumentsAbout: Where the game keeps input.settings (key bindings), mods.settings (mod priorities) and scriptslog.txt. It's Documents\The Witcher 3 on Windows; set it when your game writes elsewhere, such as under Proton or Wine, or when Documents was moved.
Settings.Game.DocumentsDefaultTip: Put Documents\The Witcher 3 back in the box
Settings.Game.DocumentsNoSettings: The game hasn't written its settings there yet: start the game once, or choose where it writes them.
Settings.Game.DocumentsNotYet: {folder} doesn't exist yet: the game makes it the first time it runs.
Settings.Game.DocumentsPick: Choose the folder the game keeps its settings in
Settings.Game.WccAbout: REDkit's own tool, for compiling scripts the way publishing from REDkit does. REDkit's source files, found beside it, also fill in the properties cooking leaves out of the game's files.
Settings.Game.WccFindTip: Look for REDkit in your Steam and GOG libraries
Settings.Game.WccHint: REDkit is free on Steam and GOG for owners of the game. wcc_lite is in its bin\x64_RedKit folder.
Settings.Game.WccNotSetBuiltIn: Not set. Compile uses the built-in compiler, which reads the game's scripts.
Settings.Game.WccNotSetNoScripts: Not set, and the game's scripts weren't found, so Compile is off. Scripts can still be edited and saved.
Settings.Game.WccFound: Found wcc_lite and REDkit's game scripts.
Settings.Game.WccNoScripts: That's wcc_lite, but REDkit's r4data\scripts folder isn't two folders up from it, where it's expected.
Settings.Game.WccWrongFile: Choose wcc_lite.exe in REDkit's bin\x64_RedKit folder.
Settings.Game.WccMissing: It isn't in your Steam or GOG libraries. Use the folder button to pick wcc_lite.exe yourself.
Settings.Game.MergerAbout: Script Merger Remastered by relapse12, which merges mods that change the same scripts or files. The load order analyser suggests it for clashes and opens it from a button.
Settings.Game.MergerFindTip: Look in the game folder, Documents and Downloads
Settings.Game.MergerHint: It's a separate download (nexusmods.com/witcher3/mods/13076). This app only starts it; it doesn't bundle or change it.
Settings.Game.MergerNotSet: Not set. The load order analyser still works; it just can't open the merger for you.
Settings.Game.MergerWrongFile: That isn't a program. Choose the merger's .exe.
Settings.Game.MergerMissing: It isn't in the game folder, Documents or Downloads. Use the folder button to pick its .exe yourself.

Settings.Language.AppWindowsTip: The language Windows shows, when the app has it, else English
Settings.Language.AppStatusWindows: Windows shows {windows}, so the app is in {language}.
Settings.Language.Pseudo: Pseudo-locale, for testing: English accented and lengthened, to find text that isn't localised and layouts that clip
Settings.Language.AppHint: Windows, menus and messages change as soon as you save. Text a window has already filled in changes when it's opened again or the app restarts. The guide (F1) shows the pages translated into your language and the rest in English.
Settings.Language.GameIntro: The language of the game's text and voices the viewers start in. Each viewer's own language list can still change it for a while.
Settings.Language.GameNotFound: The game wasn't found, so it can't be said which languages it has.

Settings.Language.HasTextOnly: Your game has {language} text, and no {language} voices: scenes use the English voices.

Settings.Language.HasNone: Your game hasn't {language} installed: lines and voices show in English. Steam and GOG install other languages from the game's properties.

Settings.Language.UsedForCutscenes: •  Cutscenes: their lines. Their voices stay English, as the animation and lip sync are timed to them.
Settings.Language.UsedForStrings: •  The game strings search, and the strings editor when a file doesn't say its language.
Settings.Scripts.Intro: How scripts are compiled, how files open, and how the code editors look and help.
Settings.Scripts.CompilerAuto: wcc_lite when it's set, else the built-in compiler
Settings.Scripts.CompilerHint: The built-in compiler takes a second and needs only the game's scripts. wcc_lite takes about a minute and is the game's own, so use it for a release. Both write the same precompiled.rsblob.
Settings.Scripts.WillUseBuiltIn: Compile will use the built-in compiler.
Settings.Scripts.WillUseNeither: Neither compiler can run: the game's scripts weren't found. Set the game folder under Game and tools.
Settings.Scripts.OpenHint: For the files that open in the preview window, such as text and strings. Scripts always open in Script Bench. A file that's open already is brought forward instead of opening twice.
Settings.Scripts.EditorsHint: For scripts, XML and stubs. The game's own scripts are indented with tabs, so the tab width is how far in their code sits. JSON keeps its two spaces.
Settings.Scripts.Peek: Show a name's declaration when the mouse rests on it in a script
Settings.Scripts.Complete: Suggest names while typing in a script (Ctrl+Space suggests them any time)
Settings.Scripts.CheckAsYouType: Check your project's scripts as you type, and underline what's wrong
Settings.Scripts.CheckAsYouTypeHint: A moment after you stop typing, the built-in compiler checks your project's scripts as Compile would, with the changes you haven't saved. What's wrong gets a wavy red line, and the count in Script Bench's status bar lists it all. The game's scripts and your installed mods are read once, when Script Bench opens.
Settings.Scripts.ParameterHintsHint: Shows which parameter each argument fills, before it: Heal(amount: 10). While Ctrl+Alt is held keeps the code as it is until you want to look.
Settings.Scripts.DimUnused: Fade locals, parameters and private fields that are never used
Settings.Scripts.DimUnusedHint: A parameter the function can't do without (an event's, a timer's, or one a wrapped or overridden function must keep) isn't faded.
Settings.Scripts.FormattingIntro: How Format document (Shift+Alt+F) lays a script out. The defaults are the game's own scripts' style.
Settings.Scripts.FormatBraceOwnLine: {{ on a line of its own
Settings.Scripts.FormatBraceSameLine: {{ at the end of the line
Settings.Scripts.FormatKeepAlignment: Keep the spaces that line declarations up with each other, as the game's scripts do
Settings.Scripts.FormatAlignColons: Line up the colons of a class's fields declared one after another
Settings.Scripts.FormatOnSave: Format a script of your project each time it's saved
Settings.Scripts.FormattingHint: Formatting changes only spaces, indentation and line breaks. It checks that every word, number, string and comment stays as it was, and leaves the file alone if anything else would change.
Settings.Viewers.Intro: What the viewers read, and how much detail the 3D views load.
Settings.Viewers.RedkitProps: Read them from REDkit's source files when REDkit has one
Settings.Viewers.RedkitPropsHint: Cooking leaves out what the game doesn't need to run, such as defaults and editor notes, which REDkit's source copies keep. Off, the viewers show the game's cooked file only, exactly as the game reads it. A mod's or your project's files always show their own.
Settings.Viewers.RedkitMissing: REDkit isn't installed or found, so the viewers show the game's cooked files either way.
Settings.Viewers.AntialiasingHint: How smooth the edges of meshes are drawn (multisample anti-aliasing). 4× is smoothest but costs the graphics card the most: a mesh filling a big window can drop to half the frame rate. 2× suits most. Applies to views opened next.
Settings.Viewers.SimulateCloth: Simulate cloth as the game does
Settings.Viewers.SimulateClothHint: Capes, skirts, coat tails and flags (.redcloth) swing and hang with gravity, are pushed by the body and collide with it, using the cloth's own settings, in the entity, scene, cutscene and animation views. Off, cloth moves stiffly with the bones like any other mesh, which is quicker with a big cast. The cloth viewer always simulates. Applies to views opened next.
Settings.Viewers.TextureDetailHint: The largest a texture is read for entities, scenes, cutscenes, rigs and animations. Higher is sharper close up but slower to load, and a scene with many actors uses much more memory. Medium suits most. Viewers open already keep what they've read; it applies to those opened next.
Settings.Viewers.ExportLodsHint: Which LODs the mesh viewer's Export puts in a .glb. Every LOD gives each one a node of its own (name_lod0, name_lod1…), on top of each other, for remaking them all; the LOD shown is all most edits need. The chunks unticked in the viewer are left out either way. An .obj always has the LOD shown only.
Settings.Viewers.ExportTexturesHint: Each material's colour, its normal map and the roughness the game keeps in the normal map's alpha, at full size, so Blender and other tools show the mesh as it looks. Off, the file is much smaller, and the textures' game paths are still kept with each material.
Settings.Viewers.ImportLodsHint: When a .glb imported onto a mesh has no parts for one of the mesh's LODs (a file of LOD 0 only, say), whether that LOD is the file's nearest LOD below it, so the change shows from every distance, or the mesh's own, which is lighter far away but shows the old shape there. A LOD the mesh draws nothing in is always kept.
Settings.Viewers.MakeMod: Making a mod of a game file
Settings.Viewers.MakeModPicturesHint: What Make a mod copies textures as, for you to edit: .png and .tga open in any picture editor (.tga keeps the alpha channel plainly), .dds keeps the game's compression and mip levels and needs an editor that reads .dds. Build makes each into the game's texture again, with the game's settings for it. Cube maps and texture arrays always go in as .dds.
Settings.Viewers.MakeModOpen: Open the copy of the file once it is in the project
Settings.Viewers.SoundUpgradeReplace: Replace the cache or bank, keeping the original as .bak
Settings.Viewers.SoundUpgradeReplaceHint: What Upgrade sounds to v150 does with what it makes. On, it replaces the file, and the original stays beside it with .bak on the end (rename it back to undo). Off, it asks where to save a new file.
Settings.Viewers.SpeechUnpackWav: Save a .wav of each voice line when unpacking a speech file
Settings.Viewers.SpeechUnpackWavHint: Voice lines (Tools) always saves each line's .wem, as the game keeps it. A .wav as well is for listening or editing in any sound editor; it doesn't go back in the game.

Settings.Privacy.EabAbout: EasyAssetBrowser's community categories and tags for the game's files, shown in the Asset Browser. They're downloaded from its GitHub repository about once a day, which GitHub sees as any download. Nothing is sent.

Settings.Privacy.EabOff: Off: the app doesn't go online at all.

Settings.Privacy.PrivacySummary: W3 Mod Workbench collects no information about you. It works offline and goes online only for EasyAssetBrowser tags, which are off until you turn them on: it then downloads their lists from GitHub, which sees your IP address as with any download.

FileKinds.Ws.Description: Script source: classes, functions and states the game compiles at start-up.
FileKinds.Rsblob.Description: Scripts compiled by REDkit. The tool decompiles them back to WitcherScript.
FileKinds.Xml.Description: Game data: items, abilities, menus, loot and more, read when the game starts.
FileKinds.Csv.Description: A table of data, such as strings for one language, or a list the game looks things up in.
FileKinds.W3strings.Description: The game's text for one language, each line under a number that scripts and data refer to.
FileKinds.Json.Description: Settings or data in plain text, such as a mod's info.json.
FileKinds.Settings.Description: Plain-text settings, such as input.settings or mods.settings.
FileKinds.W2mesh.Description: A 3D model: its materials, LODs and how it's split up. The shape itself is in the .buffer files beside it.
FileKinds.Buffer.Description: The bulk data of the file it's named after, such as a mesh's vertices. Only that file can read it, so keep the two together.
FileKinds.W2ent.Description: A template for something in the world: an NPC, a monster, an item or a piece of armour, with its components.
FileKinds.W2rig.Description: A skeleton: the bones a model is skinned to and that animations move.
FileKinds.W2animev.Description: Events timed to animations: sounds, effects, footsteps and hits.
FileKinds.W2ragdoll.Description: How a body falls and collides when it goes limp.
FileKinds.W2p.Description: A visual effect made of particles: fire, sparks, blood, magic.
FileKinds.Redfur.Description: Hair and fur, drawn with NVIDIA HairWorks.
FileKinds.Redcloth.Description: Simulated cloth, such as capes and skirts.
FileKinds.Apb.Description: Simulated cloth made with NVIDIA APEX.
FileKinds.Srt.Description: A tree or plant made with SpeedTree.
FileKinds.Xbm.Description: A texture's description. In a mod or the game its pixels are in a texture.cache under the same path.
FileKinds.Dds.Description: A texture with its mip levels, as graphics tools and the game's cooker read them.
FileKinds.Png.Description: A picture, usually a texture before it's cooked or an icon.
FileKinds.Tga.Description: A picture, usually a texture before it's cooked.
FileKinds.W2mi.Description: A material with its settings filled in: which textures and colours a surface uses.
FileKinds.W2mg.Description: A shader: how a kind of surface is drawn.
FileKinds.W2cube.Description: A texture of the surroundings, for reflections and the sky.
FileKinds.Texarray.Description: Several textures of the same size kept as one, such as terrain layers.
FileKinds.Env.Description: Lighting, fog, sky and colour grading for an area or a time of day.
FileKinds.W2w.Description: A world's settings: its terrain, sky and the layers of things placed in it.
FileKinds.W2l.Description: Things placed in a world together: buildings, NPCs, triggers, lights.
FileKinds.W2ter.Description: A piece of a world's ground.
FileKinds.Flyr.Description: The grass, bushes and trees placed on a piece of a world.
FileKinds.W3simplex.Description: A world's map cut by straight lines into areas: where the wind is damped, where water can be seen from.
FileKinds.W2dset.Description: Where the actors of a dialogue stand and the cameras that film them.
FileKinds.W2quest.Description: The top of a quest: its phases and how they connect.
FileKinds.W2phase.Description: A step of a quest: the blocks that run its scenes, objectives and facts.
FileKinds.W2scene.Description: A conversation or cutscene: lines, cameras, animations and choices.
FileKinds.W2cutscene.Description: A recorded cutscene, played as it is: its actors, their animations and the camera's, and events timed along them.
FileKinds.W2comm.Description: NPCs who live somewhere: who they are, where they go and when.
FileKinds.W2job.Description: Something an NPC does in place, such as sweeping or sitting, as a run of animations.
FileKinds.W2beh.Description: How a character's animations blend and change from one to another.
FileKinds.W2behtree.Description: An NPC's or monster's AI: what it decides to do and when.
FileKinds.Journal.Description: A page of the journal: a quest, a character, a creature or a glossary entry.
FileKinds.Reddlc.Description: Says what a DLC adds to the game, and when.
FileKinds.Redswf.Description: A menu or HUD panel: a Flash movie the game shows and scripts talk to.
FileKinds.Bnk.Description: Wwise sounds and the events that play them.
FileKinds.Wem.Description: A Wwise sound: speech, music or an effect.
FileKinds.Usm.Description: A video, such as an intro or an ending.
FileKinds.Subs.Description: A video's subtitles in one language: each line with when it shows and goes.
FileKinds.Bundle.Description: An archive of the game's or a mod's files.
FileKinds.Cache.Description: An archive of textures, sounds, collision or shaders.
FileKinds.BufferOf: The bulk data of {file} ({kind}). Only that file can read it, so keep the two together.

LoadOrderAnalyzer.PreferAnnotationsWrapM: Prefer annotations (@wrapMethod and friends) where the mod can be rewritten to use them.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.EachDeclareScriptsUse: {ranked} each declare the {kind} {key}. Scripts that use it get whichever the game loads, and the other mod's code expects a different shape.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.OnlyOneTheseMods: Only one of these mods can be installed, unless one is changed to use a different name.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ModsCompiledScriptsDec: The mod's compiled scripts declare {kind} {key}, which the game already has, so its version takes the game's place and hides other mods' additions to it.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ValuesMayDifferWhich: The values may differ, which breaks code compiled against the other mod's number.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.GiveDifferentNamesNumb: {ranked} give different names the number {key} in {enumName}.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.SavedGamesCodeComparin: Saved games and code comparing the number will read the wrong value.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.GlobalFunctionDefinedM: Global function {key}() is defined by {mods} mods
LoadOrderAnalyzer.DeclareOnlyOneDefiniti: {ranked} declare it. Only one definition can exist.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.RenameOneThemRemove: Rename one of them or remove one of the mods.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.EachAddClassCant: {ranked} each add the {kind} {target}. A class can't have it twice, so one of them fails.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.RenameMemberOneMods: Rename the member in one of the mods, or remove one.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.EachUseReplaceMethodOn: {ranked} each use @replaceMethod. Only one replacement runs; the other mod's version of {target} is thrown away.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.KeepOneIfBoth: Keep one. If both are wanted, Script Merger Remastered may be able to merge them, or one mod has to be rewritten with @wrapMethod.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ReplacedWrapped: {target} is replaced by {name} and wrapped by {count}
LoadOrderAnalyzer.CheckGameBothMods: Check in game that both mods still work. A replace that loads after a wrap usually discards it; Script Merger Remastered can combine such changes.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.EachWrapWrapsStack: {ranked} each wrap it. Wraps stack, each calling the one below, so this normally works. It breaks only if one of them forgets to call wrappedMethod() or changes the result the other expects.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.NoActionUnlessOne: No action unless one of the mods misbehaves; then try changing their order.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ModProbablyWrittenAnot: The mod was probably written for another game version, or needs a mod that isn't installed or enabled.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.WrapsReplacesGameDoesn: {name} wraps or replaces {count} the game doesn't have
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ClassesExistButThese: The classes exist, but these functions are not declared in them (or their base classes) by the game or any enabled mod. The mod was most likely written for a different version of the game, and these will fail to compile or never run.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.GetVersionModMade: Get a version of the mod made for this game version, or remove it.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.NoGlobalFunctionThese: No global function of these names exists in the game's scripts or an enabled mod.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.CopyGameClassLacks: {name}'s copy of a game class lacks what {name2} changes
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ReplacesGamesClassWhol: {name} replaces the game's class whole, and its version has no such function. {name2}'s annotations have nothing to attach to.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.UpdateReplacementGames: Update the replacement from the game's current script, or use annotations instead of replacing the file.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.UsesOnlyProvidesMods: {name} uses {count} that only {name2} provides, and mods.settings has {name2} switched off.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.LoadsBeforeWhichBuilds: {name} loads before {name2}, which builds on it
LoadOrderAnalyzer.UsesGameCompilesScript: {name} (#{order}) uses {count} from {name2} (#{order2}). The game compiles scripts in reverse load order, so the mod that provides them has to load last. As it is this tends to end in "Unknown base class" or "different number of parameters" errors when the game starts.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.OnlyOneHasPriority: Only one of {name} and {name2} has a priority
LoadOrderAnalyzer.HasPriorityModsSetting: {name} has priority {priority} in mods.settings and the other has none. Mixing the two makes the compile order depend on how the tool treats unlisted mods, and {name2} uses {count} from {name3}.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.GiveBothPriorityMod: Give both a priority, with the mod that provides the scripts the higher number (200 or 1000 is fine), or remove priorities from both and let the folder names decide.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.UsesWhichInstalledEnab: {name} uses {count} from {name2}, which is installed, enabled and in the right place in the order (it loads after, so it compiles first).
LoadOrderAnalyzer.NothingDoKeepBoth: Nothing to do. Keep both installed.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.CompiledScriptsLinkThe: Its compiled scripts link to these classes or functions, but neither the game nor any enabled mod declares them. A mod it depends on is probably not installed, or it was written for a different game version.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.InstallModNeedsMods: Install the mod it needs (the mod's page lists its requirements), or remove this one.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.GiveHigherPriorityNumb: Give {name} a higher priority number than {name2} (200 or 1000 is fine; both need one), or remove priorities from both and let folder names decide: a prefix such as modzzz sorts last, so it compiles first.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ModsInfoJsonLists: The mod's info.json lists {declared} as a dependency, but no installed mod or DLC matches it.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ModsInfoJsonLists2: The mod's info.json lists it as a dependency.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.LoadsBeforeWhichDeclar: {name} loads before {name2}, which declares it as a dependency
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ScriptsCompileReverseL: {name} is #{order} and {name2} #{order2}. Scripts compile in reverse load order, so a dependency has to load after the mods that use it.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.AlsoBundlesCovered: {count} also in the bundles of {count2}, covered by {name}
LoadOrderAnalyzer.EachContainTheseFiles: {ranked} each contain these files with different content. {name} loads first and is a merge, so it should already combine them.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.EachContainTheseFiles2: {ranked} each contain these files with different content. The game uses one copy per file: {first}'s, the highest priority, in each case. The others' changes to them are lost.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.DecideWhichModsVersion: Decide which mod's version you want, or let Script Merger Remastered combine them where it can (Open Script Merger, below).
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ShipByteIdenticalCopie: {ranked} ship byte-identical copies of these files, so it doesn't matter which one is used.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.UsedModsDifferentText: {count} used by {mods} mods with different text
LoadOrderAnalyzer.EachDefineStringsSame: {ranked} each define strings with the same IDs. The game shows one text for an ID, so one mod's text appears where the other's belongs.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MoveOneModsStrings: Move one mod's strings to a free ID block (the strings editor's Check IDs suggests one).
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MostCompiledScriptsSay: Most compiled scripts say they were built for {key}.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ScriptsBuiltAnotherPla: Scripts built for another platform may not load. Get the version made for this game.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ModsSettingsWasntFound: mods.settings wasn't found (Documents\The Witcher 3), so priorities are mod folder order. Run the game once, or set the file in the box above.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ModsSettingsGivesEach: mods.settings gives each mod a priority. These have none, so they load after the listed mods, in folder name order. For script mods leaving priorities out is the recommended way.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.NothingUnlessOneThem: Nothing, unless one of them also needs a priority: a mod with a priority and a dependency without one is flagged separately.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.EqualPrioritiesFallBac: Equal priorities fall back to folder name order.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.GiveEachDifferentNumbe: Give each a different number if it matters which one wins.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ModsSettingsModsArent: {count} in mods.settings for mods that aren't installed
LoadOrderAnalyzer.PrioritiesModsYouRemov: Priorities of mods you removed stay behind and still shape the compile order, which has caused "Unknown base class" errors for other players.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.DeleteTheseSectionsMod: Delete these sections from mods.settings (the mod manager's Mod Settings tab shows the same file).
LoadOrderAnalyzer.TheseArentLoadedSo: These aren't loaded, so they are left out of every check here except dependencies.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.Report.Title: Load order report
LoadOrderAnalyzer.DifferentVersionsGame: {mods} each ship a different version of a game script. Only one is used: {first}, the highest priority. The others' changes in that file are lost.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.DifferentVersionsFile: {mods} each ship a different version of this file. Only one is used: {first}, the highest priority. The others' changes in that file are lost.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ReplaceAndWraps: @replaceMethod swaps out the whole body; whether the wraps around it still run depends on the order the mods are applied. {mod} is #{order}.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.ReplaceAndWrapsLater: @replaceMethod swaps out the whole body; whether the wraps around it still run depends on the order the mods are applied. {mod} is #{order}, {later} come after it.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MissingClasses: Its annotations name classes that neither the game nor any enabled mod declares, so they have nothing to attach to.

LoadOrderAnalyzer.MissingClassesDisabled.one: Its annotations name classes that neither the game nor any enabled mod declares, so they have nothing to attach to. {mods} declare some, but is disabled.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MissingClassesDisabled.other: Its annotations name classes that neither the game nor any enabled mod declares, so they have nothing to attach to. {mods} declare some, but are disabled.

LoadOrderAnalyzer.TexturesDifferSummary: {ranked} each have these textures in their texture.cache, made differently. The game shows {first}'s, the highest priority; the others' are never seen.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.TexturesDifferAdvice: Decide which mod's look you want and give it the higher priority. A texture only shows right with its own mod's .xbm, so a mod's textures and its bundles should win together.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.TexturesSameSummary: {ranked} have byte-identical copies of these textures, so whichever wins looks the same.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.TextureMismatchSummary: The game takes these textures' .xbm from {xbmMod} and their pixels from {cacheMod}'s texture.cache, which has them at another size or format than {xbmMod}'s own. A texture whose .xbm and pixels don't match shows garbled, stretched or black, and can crash the game.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.TextureMismatchAdvice: Give {xbmMod} and {cacheMod} priorities so that one mod wins both its .xbm and its pixels, or remove one of them.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.DlcIdShared: DLC ID {id} is used by {count} mods
LoadOrderAnalyzer.DlcIdSharedSummary: {ranked} each declare a DLC with the ID {id} in a .reddlc. The game mounts one DLC per ID, so all but one are left out: their quests, items and places aren't there.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.DlcIdSharedAdvice: Two mods with one DLC ID are usually two versions of the same mod, or one mod built from another: keep one. If they're different mods, ask an author to give theirs an ID of its own.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuBroken: The menu file {file} isn't valid XML
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuBrokenSummary: {file} in the game's menu folder ({path}) can't be read. The game reads every file there to build its options menus, and one it can't read can leave a mod's menu, or the whole Options menu, empty.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuBrokenAdvice: Open {file} and fix the line the error names (often an & that should be &, or a tag that is never closed), or put back the copy from the mod's download.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuGroupTwice: The menu group {id} is in {count} files
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuGroupTwiceSummary: The options menu group {id} is defined in {files}. The game shows one of them, so settings only the other has aren't shown and can't be changed.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuGroupTwiceAdvice: Usually an old and a new copy of one mod's menu: delete the old file. Two different mods sharing a group need one of them to rename theirs.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuMissingSummary: {mod}'s scripts read their settings from the options menu group {groups}, but no menu file in the game's bin\config\r4game\user_config_matrix\pc defines it. Every setting reads as empty, so the mod may do nothing, or behave as if everything were switched off.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuMissingAdvice: Copy the bin folder from {mod}'s download into the game's folder (it holds the menu's .xml), or install the mod again with a mod manager that copies it. If the group is another mod's, install that mod.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuOld: {mod} reads {settings} its menu file hasn't got
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuOldSummary: {mod}'s scripts read these settings from its options menu, but the menu file installed hasn't got them: it's from another version of the mod. The missing settings read as empty.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.MenuOldAdvice: Copy the menu .xml from the bin folder of the {mod} you have installed into the game's folder, over the old one.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.NoInputSettings: input.settings wasn't found in Documents\The Witcher 3, so mods' keys weren't checked
LoadOrderAnalyzer.KeysMissingSummary: {mod}'s scripts listen for these input actions, but {path} has no line for them, so no key does them and the mod's hotkeys do nothing.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.KeysMissingAdvice: Add the lines from {mod}'s readme to input.settings (with the game closed), then set the keys in the game's key bindings menu if the mod adds them there. Tools > Key binding helper shows what the lines look like.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.KeysUnsetSummary: input.settings lists these actions of {mod}, but on IK_None: no key is set for them.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.KeysUnsetAdvice: Set a key in the game's key bindings menu if the action is listed there, or change IK_None to a key in input.settings.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.KeysSharedSummary: In input.settings these keys do a mod's action and another action in the same context, so pressing one does both.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.KeysSharedAdvice: Move one of the actions to a free key in the game's key bindings menu or in input.settings. Some mods share a key with the game on purpose, to do something more when it's pressed; their readme says so.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.XmlClashSummary: {ranked} each set these XML definitions (items, abilities and the like) to different values. The game uses {winner}'s: XML loads in its own order, by the name of the DLC folder that mounts it, not by mod priority.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.XmlClashAdvice: Decide which values you want. Tools > View XML overrides shows every definition and field, and Script Merger Remastered can merge the XML files.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.XmlCouldntRead: The mods' XML couldn't be read: {error}
LoadOrderAnalyzer.SomeCombinable: In {combinable} of the {total} files the mods change different things, so one file could hold both.
LoadOrderAnalyzer.FileSameAsGame: {mod}'s copy is the same as the game's
LoadOrderAnalyzer.FileCombinable: they change different things: one file could hold both mods' changes
LoadOrderAnalyzer.FileNewDiffers: a file the game hasn't got: {first}'s and {second}'s copies differ in {properties}
ModDownload.UnpackFirst: {file} isn't a .zip: unpack it first (a .7z or .rar with 7-Zip, say) and pick its folder.
ModDownload.NoMod: There's no mod in {name}: a mod is a folder named mod… or dlc… with a content folder in it, usually under mods\ or dlc\.

CompareWindow.Name: Name
CompareWindow.DifferenceTip: One picture: the left one in grey, with every pixel that differs in magenta
CompareWindow.NoDifferencesText: Everything is the same on both sides. Untick Only differences to see it all.
CompareWindow.NothingMatchesText: Nothing's name or value has that in it.
CompareWindow.DifferenceInfo: {left} in grey, where {right} differs in magenta

CompareWindow.PictureMissing: One side has no picture to show

CompareWindow.WithGameTip: This is a copy of a game file: see what it changes from the game's own, side by side
CompareWindow.CopiesTip: Pick a file both mods ship to see their two copies side by side
CompareWindow.TwoTip: Compare the two highlighted files side by side
ComparePick.Title: Compare files
ComparePick.Explain: Pick two files to see what differs between them: entities, meshes and other game files property by property, strings by ID, textures as pictures, compiled scripts and text line by line. Each side is a file on disk, or a game path like characters\npc_entities\animals\horse\horse.w2ent read from the game.
ComparePick.BoxTip: A file on disk (Browse, type its path, or drop it here), or a game path to read from the game. Drop two files to fill both sides.
ComparePick.NotFound: {file} isn't a file on disk or in the game.
ModMaker.ButtonTip: Copy this file into your project, ready to change, with what it's made of: its meshes, materials, and textures as pictures to edit
ModMaker.Title: Make a mod
ModMaker.Explain: Copies it into your project at its game path, with the files it's made of that you tick. Textures go in as pictures to edit, which Build makes into the game's textures again. The game's own files are never changed.
ModMaker.NoProject: No project is open: you'll be asked to make one or open one.
ModMaker.NeedsProject: A mod made from a game file goes in a project.
ModMaker.TexturesHint: Each goes in as a picture beside its game path; Build makes it into the texture with the game's format, size and mip levels.
ModMaker.OtherHint: Animations, behaviour, rigs and the like: not copied unless you tick them.
ModMaker.SharedHint: Files much of the game uses: changing one changes everything that uses it, so they're left out. Tick one only if that's what you mean to do.
ModMaker.SharedGraph: a material graph every material on it uses
ModMaker.SharedBase: a base entity many entities build on
ModMaker.NoPixels: the game's texture caches have no pixels for it
ModMaker.FormatTip: What the textures go in as. .png and .tga open in any picture editor; .dds keeps the compression and mip levels
ModMaker.Copied: {files} copied into {project}, at their game paths in its workspace.
ModMaker.CopiedBuffers: Their meshes' vertices came with them: {buffers}.
ModMaker.CopiedPictures: {textures} went in as pictures. Edit them in any picture editor and Build makes them into the game's textures.
ModMaker.CopiedExisting: {files} the project had already were left as they are.
ItemEditor.Title: Item editor
ItemEditor.Explain: Every item of the game, with its stats, the schematics and recipes that make it and where it's found. Change any value; Save writes your changes into the project: items and their stats as XML overrides in the project's own DLC, which work beside other mods, and schematics and loot in copies of the game's files.
ItemEditor.NoProject: Open or make a project to change items: what you change is saved in it.
ItemEditor.NeedsProject: Changes to items are saved in a project.
ItemEditor.NoGame: The game wasn't found, so there are no items to show. Set its folder in Settings.
ItemEditor.Search: Search by name, in-game name or tag  (Ctrl+F)
ItemEditor.ChangedOnlyTip: Only the items your project changes, or whose stats, schematics or loot it changes
ItemEditor.ChangedTip: Your project changes this item, its stats or how it is made
ItemEditor.GeneralHint: The item's own attributes. Changing these alone saves as on_conflict="extend", just what you changed; changing its tags or base abilities saves the whole item as on_conflict="replace".
ItemEditor.AbilityOwn: This ability is the item's own. It saves whole, as on_conflict="replace".
ItemEditor.AbilityShared: This ability is given to {items}: changing it changes all of them. It saves whole, as on_conflict="replace".
ItemEditor.AbilityNotFound: This ability isn't in the game's XML.
ItemEditor.WholeFile: The game can't take an override for this, so changing it saves a copy of {file} with this definition changed; another mod changing the same file would clash with it.
ItemEditor.NotMade: No schematic or recipe makes this item.
ItemEditor.NotFoundAnywhere: This item isn't in any loot table.
ItemEditor.PutBackTip: Put this definition back as the game has it
ItemEditor.AlsoNewGamePlusTip: Make the same changes to New Game+'s copies, which keep their own values otherwise (its stronger stats stay as they are)
ItemEditor.SaveTip: Write your changes into the project (Ctrl+S); Build makes them into the mod and its DLC
ItemEditor.Saved: {files} saved, {overrides} of them overrides in the DLC {dlc}.
ItemEditor.UnsavedText: Your changes to items aren't saved in the project yet.
ItemEdits.NotFoundAt: The definition <{tag}> wasn't found at line {line} of the file.
ItemEdits.NotClosed: The definition <{tag}> isn't closed in the file.
MenuModel.IsntModMenuFirst: This isn't a mod menu: its first element isn't <UserConfig>.
MenuModel.MenuHasNoPages: The menu has no pages yet.
MenuModel.PageHasNoId: A page has no id: scripts need it to read the page's settings.
MenuModel.PageHasNoDisplay: Page '{id}' has no display name, so it won't show in the menu.
MenuModel.SettingHasNoId: A setting in '{id}' has no id.
MenuModel.AnotherSettingPageHas: {at}: another setting on this page has the same id.
MenuModel.IdsSpacesSymbolsHard: {at}: ids with spaces or symbols are hard to read from a script. Letters, digits and _ are safest.
MenuModel.NoDisplayNameSo: {at}: no display name, so the menu would show nothing for it.
MenuModel.TogglesDefaultHasTrue: {at}: a toggle's default has to be true or false.
MenuModel.SlidersEndsHaveNumbers: {at}: the slider's ends have to be numbers.
MenuModel.SlidersMinimumHasBelow: {at}: the slider's minimum has to be below its maximum.
MenuModel.SlidersStepsHaveNumber: {at}: the slider's steps have to be a number above 0.
MenuModel.OptionsSettingNeedsLeast: {at}: an options setting needs at least one option.
MenuModel.DefaultIsntOneOptions: {at}: the default {default} isn't one of the options.
MenuModel.PresetSetsWhichIsnt: '{id}' / preset {id2}: sets '{varId}', which isn't a setting on this page.
ClothFile.ClothsShapeWasntFound: The cloth's shape wasn't found: it's kept in the game's collision.cache, which wasn't found.
ClothFile.ClothsShapeIsntApex: The cloth's shape isn't an APEX asset this tool can read.
ClothFile.ClothsRenderMeshWasnt: The cloth's render mesh wasn't found in its APEX asset.
ClothFile.SettingNotSet: The cloth's {name} setting couldn't be written into the file.
ClothFile.ApexAssetCutShort: The APEX asset is cut short.
ClothFile.CollisionCachesIndexOut: The collision cache's index is out of its file.
MaterialWriter.ParameterHasValueCant: The parameter {name} has a value that can't be written.
MaterialWriter.TheresNoMaterialInstance: There's no material instance in this file.
MaterialWriter.MeshHasNoMaterial: The mesh has no material list to change.
MeshFile.NotMesh: This is a {className}, not a mesh.
MeshFile.TheresNoMeshFile: There's no mesh in this file.

MeshFile.MeshKeepsShapeWay: This mesh keeps its shape in a way that can't be read yet: it has no cooked data and no raw vertices.
MeshFile.MeshsChunkTableShorter: The mesh's chunk table is shorter than it says.
MeshFile.MeshsBufferShorterThan: The mesh's buffer is shorter than its chunks say.
ModPacker.CouldntCookedGoes: {gamePath} couldn't be cooked ({message}); it goes in as it is
ModPacker.LeftOutSoundCache: {gamePath} is left out: the sound cache has a {name} already (sounds go by their file name alone)

ModPacker.VoiceLinesInWith: {0} in {1} ({2} from the project's speech folder, the rest from the speech file at the workspace's top)
ModPacker.WorkspaceLeftOutBuild: {name} in the workspace is left out: the build made its own {name} from the workspace's files
ModPacker.ContentWorkspaceHas: content\{name}, as the workspace has it
ModPacker.MipLevelsIn: the mip levels of {textures} in content\{file}
Pictures.OnlyTrueColourGreyscale: only true-colour and greyscale .tga files can be used

TextureReplacer.CantUse: The picture can't be made into this texture

TextureReplacer.PreviewSource: made from your picture, as Build will

TextureCooker.OldCube: This is a cube from an early REDkit, which keeps its faces another way; it's packed as it is.
TextureCooker.CubeShort: The cube's faces are shorter than its levels say.
TextureCooker.ArrayNoSlices: The texture array names no bitmaps for its slices.
TextureCooker.ArraySliceMissing: The texture array's slice {texture} wasn't found in the project or the game.

SoundUpgrade.Title: Upgrade sounds to v150
SoundUpgrade.Intro: The Remastered plays only sound banks of version 150. This rewrites a mod's banks made for the original game (88) or the next-gen update (140) as 150, and gives its streamed sounds the header the Remastered reads. Every rule it follows was learnt from the game's own banks, not guessed; what it can't upgrade it keeps as it was and says why.
